name: finish-solo-002
prompt:
Create an ORIGINAL FORMA fitness manual illustration, ONE scene only landscape1536x1024. Whitebackground, subtle shadow, crisp precise charcoalgray sportswear/equipment and tiny limegreen accents. Anatomically correct fully clothed adult with exactly2arms2legs, entire head/body/hands/feet plus entire bench and both dumbbells within canvas with60pxmargin. No labels, words, logos, arrows, borders or watermarks.
SUBJECT: Flexor Incline Dumbbell Curls, bilateral MID-CURL working phase. Athlete seated against incline bench with FULL BACK AND HEAD SUPPORTED on backrest. Bench BACKREST is EXACTLY45degrees above horizontal floor: its vertical rise equals its horizontal run in near-orthographic SIDE view. Long pad slopes diagonally up-left from pelvis to head, not steep60degrees and not low30degrees. Seat separate and horizontal, knees bent feet planted flatfloor in front. Camera is near SIDE orthographic from front-right just enough to see BOTH independent arms and hands; avoid foreshortening bench slope.
Both upper arms hang downward close to body, elbows beside ribs fixed. Both forearms curl forward up until roughlyHORIZONTAL in midphase, ONE separate dumbbell in EACH hand. BOTH PALMS visibly SUPINATED UPWARD, thumbs pointing outward away from body and no wrist twisting.
DEFINING WRISTS: BOTH wrists visibly EXTENDED/BENT BACK, not straight aligned with forearm. Show clear dorsal extension at each wrist; hand/palm tilts back/down relative to upward forearm so wrist angle unmistakable. Each dumbbell is held on a LONG exposed horizontal grip shaft OFFSET TOWARD OUTER end FARTHER FROM ATHLETE. Each fist sits close to OUTER weight head: the longer remaining shaft and more of weight assembly lie toward athlete/INNER side. Do NOT center hands on grip. Both off-centre grips clearly visible with fingers contacting shaft right beside outer head and obvious longer bare shaft between fist and inner head. Standard compact round dumbbell weight heads with long handles for clear eccentric grip; no kettlebells or barbell.
Make BOTH extended wrists, supinated palms, OUTBOARD offset grips, independent dumbbells,45degree head-supported incline and grounded feet completely clear while preserving entire adult/apparatus.
FULL GUIDE (factual source governs): Hold the dumbbell towards the side farther from you so that you have more weight on the side closest to you. (This can be done for a good effect on all bicep dumbbell exercises). Now do a normal incline dumbbell curl, but keep your wrists as far back as possible so as to neutralize any stress that is placed on them.

Sit on an incline bench that is angled at 45-degrees while holding a dumbbell on each hand.

Let your arms hang down on your sides, with the elbows in, and turn the palms of your hands forward with the thumbs pointing away from the body. Tip: You will keep this hand position throughout the movement as there should not be any twisting of the hands as they come up. This will be your starting position.

Curl up the two dumbbells at the same time until your biceps are fully contracted and exhale. Tip: Do not swing the arms or use momentum. Keep a controlled motion at all times. Hold the contracted position for a second at the top.

As you inhale, slowly go back to the starting position.

Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
